note: Every number here is read off an artefact in this repo, and the field that names which one is `basis`. A field nobody measured is `null` with a `_unknown` entry saying so, never a plausible-looking figure - a ledger whose purpose is to make claims admissible cannot itself contain an estimate dressed as a measurement.

The first row is deliberately mostly null. That IS the first finding: of the eleven things the row schema asks for, the harness can currently produce four without a human, and it has never been asked to produce any of them.

retro: The ratchet had no pawl. Every check in the harness was a THRESHOLD check - is the frame black, is it flat, is depth in range - and not one COMPARED this render to the last known good one. Threshold checks catch catastrophes and are structurally blind to drift, which is the only thing a 'measurably better every time' claim actually turns on. Fixed 2026-09-18: goldens/, `check.ssim`, `check.check_goldens`, `verify --bless`, calibrated on two real double-renders of ad02 (1.000000 on every shot; a 5 cm camera move scores 0.827). Measured in the same session, against an assumption in ROADMAP.md: two clean runs are pixel-identical but their PNG files are not, so a file hash fails today, a pixel hash would work today, and neither survives a GPU render node - which is why the metric is SSIM.

The most expensive bug in the project - spin written into the .z Euler slot, which swung the screws like a propeller - had no numeric test, only a WARNING whose own thresholds overlap the correct behaviour (14.3-16.3 correct vs 18.1-19.5 buggy). It was testable in six lines the whole time: turning a screw must not move the axis it turns about. Now tests/spin_axis.py.

`PassProfile.frame_count` was fixed at one end only. The top-end clamp that played a 6 s shot 18% fast was made a refusal; the bottom-end clamp that plays a 2 s shot 35% SLOW on wan's 49-frame minimum survived, un-noticed, in the same function, under a docstring that said 'at the top end'. A fix that names the end it fixes should be read as naming the end it did not.
